findings.location: Notice card, first sentence, against the reason directly beneath it; and the Internal calls / State changes empty-state notes
findings.finding: A state presented as a different state. The card asserts 'No trace can be produced for this execution — a permanent answer rather than a failed fetch', and Internal calls and State changes both say the section is 'empty permanently, not yet'. The reason given for all three is a toolchain regression in the replay runtime — a defect on the recording side, which is by construction repairable by re-running the recorder. Nothing on the page supports permanence any more; a reader who returns after the regression is fixed may well find a trace. This survives independently of finding 1: deleting the recorder-blaming clause without changing the permanence claims would leave an unsupported assertion with no stated basis at all.

findings.location: Overview grid, CANONICAL row (`Yes`) and AGE row (`No timestamp published`) — adjacent rows, 30px apart
findings.finding: One tone, two opposite meanings. Both chips are byte-identical: fill #F3F3F3, border #C8C8C8, label #565656, same radius and padding. One states an affirmative fact about the transaction ('it is canonical'); the other states that a datum does not exist. Because FINALITY immediately below uses the green affirmative pill, the grid teaches the reader 'green = affirmative, grey = missing' across AGE and FINALITY, then contradicts it one row up at CANONICAL. `Yes` is also the only ordinary scalar value in the grid rendered as a chip at all — TYPE renders `public` as plain mono, COST renders plain text — so the neutral tone is spent here without encoding anything.

findings.location: `Succeeded` (page title row), `Finalized` (Overview FINALITY row), `Real Aztec mainnet data` (Overview DATA row)
findings.finding: One tone, three meanings on three different subject axes. All three badges are fill #DCFCE7, border #16A34A, text #166534 — no differentiation whatsoever. `Succeeded` is the chain's report of an execution outcome; `Finalized` is a finality state; `Real Aztec mainnet data` is a claim about the DATASET, not about this transaction, and §4 grades it as CONTENT rather than decoration because it is the only thing telling a reader the hashes exist on a network. Giving a content-grade provenance claim the same token as a routine status pill removes the one cue that would tell a reader it is a different kind of statement. findings.location: Notice card, the `Not observable` badge

resolutions.reason: P3. The two widths are a decision, not raggedness: data panels take the column (--bt-layout-container), prose panels take one shared prose width (--bt-layout-prose). This is a recorded TENSION rather than an agreement — L2 asked twice for the trace panel to be narrowed to its content (round 3) and then for one right edge (round 5), and those cannot both hold. The narrowing won because a 910px box around a 150px button and two sentences made the container outweigh the control it holds. What WAS fixed is the accidental part: the two prose panels previously sat at different widths because --bt-measure-prose is in `ch` and they were set at different font sizes; both now use one px token, so the page has two widths rather than three.

P3. The 92px vs 100px difference is margin collapsing between the trace card's box and the following section's margin-top, not a second spacing step: both are --bt-rhythm-section. Correcting it would mean giving one boundary a hand-written offset, which is the class of ad-hoc margin the rhythm roles exist to eliminate. Read and declined.

P3, and a genuine conflict between two readings from the same lens two rounds apart. Round 2's L2 reported that the badge's TEXT started 10px right of the other values and asked for text alignment; round 5's L2 reports that the badge's BOX starts 9px left of the other values and asks for box alignment. They are the same 9px and cannot both be satisfied while a badge has padding. Text alignment was kept, because the value column is read as a column of values and the badge's label is the value. Recorded rather than silently chosen.

P3. The full hash reads as an unlabelled value because it IS unlabelled — the hero's specified treatment (a copy affordance, an age, a finality badge beside it) is exactly the content VD.4 owns, and giving the line a foundations-level flourish now would decorate a hero that is about to be rebuilt around it. The typographic half is done: it sits at --bt-type-identifier-lead-size, one rung above the 14px data mono, in --bt-text-strong.

P3, and deliberate. The H1 is monospace because it IS an identifier — the change that made the page's largest type carry the page's actual subject, which three reviewers across two campaigns asked for. A mono page title beside sans section headings is the same distinction the whole product makes everywhere else: mono means machine value. Reported as a scale inconsistency; recorded as the rule.

P3. The JSON block and the identifier rung both resolve to {type.fontSize.sm}; what differs is line-height (--bt-type-code-line 1.65 against --bt-type-identifier-line 1.5), which is deliberate — code needs looser leading than an inline identifier. The 'this is the product register' signal L1 wants is real and larger than a type token: Design-System.md §7 requires syntax highlighting from the product lineage's editor tokens here, which is the one sanctioned register crossing and is VD.4/VD.5's work.

P3. 'Raw (chain-native)' is Page-Descriptions §7.2's own name for the section, and the qualifier is load-bearing — it says the payload is the chain's, not BlockTracer's. Setting the parenthetical at a secondary weight would be a per-heading exception in a heading style that is otherwise uniform. Read and declined.

P3, and correct: the fixture's calldata is empty, so this capture cannot exercise the section's density case. That is a CONTENT gap, not a design one — it is exactly what M16 (Realistic Content Corpus) exists to supply, and the campaign's own introduction says a reviewer looking at thin content reports on the emptiness. Recorded so the gap is visible when the corpus lands.

P3, criterion A8, outside the foundations scope. The observation is accurate and the cause is recorded rather than hidden: every colour in the page resolves to a codetracer-design-system brand primitive, and the web lineage deliberately introduces no new hue (docs/DESIGN-DIVERGENCES-WEB.md §2 settles the accent towards the brand precisely to avoid a third value across three lineages). Giving the light theme an identity beyond the brand ramp is a reference-parity question against the 2026 Webflow direction, which is G4 and VD.11's.

P3, criterion A9, outside the foundations scope. The observation is right — 'a moment' is the page's one unquantified quantity, and brief §9 calls an unquantified quantity an honesty failure. It is not fixable at foundations level because the honest number depends on the recorder job's real timing, which the pipeline does not yet report to the page. VD.6 owns the degraded-state copy and should quantify it or drop the claim.

P3, criterion A8, outside the foundations scope. `blocktracer-demo-gen` is not an internal identifier — it is a shipped CLI in this repository, named in the Justfile and the README, and the footer's point is provenance: this page was rendered from a named, reproducible generator rather than from a chain. That is the opposite of the M5/M9 leak VD.1 removed, which named milestones and internal architecture. Whether provenance belongs in the footer at all is a copy question for VD.6.
